title: Fasting, honestly
hookLine: the evidence on fasting for health is mixed; religious fasts are about meaning first

cards: A platter of sandwiches goes around a lunch meeting, and a coworker smiles and says, not today, thanks. A water bottle sits untouched on a desk on a hot afternoon.
A family waits by the window for sunset before anyone reaches for a date. Across the world, people go without food for reasons that have nothing to do with a diet app.
Meanwhile fasting has become a health trend, with plans and timers and big promises. Today holds both: what the research says, plainly, and what a religious fast is for.

teach.b: First, the trend. Fasting diets, skipping meals or eating only within certain hours, are sold as fixes for weight, energy and long life.

Second, the evidence, plainly: it's mixed. Some readers of the research see benefits; others see little difference from simply eating less in an ordinary way. Some of the bigger promises run ahead of what has been shown.

And fasting isn't safe for everyone: people who are pregnant, who have diabetes, or who have struggled with eating disorders are advised to talk with a doctor first. Third, what religious fasts are for.

teach.h: A FAST TO WARD OFF EVIL.
teach.b: The Qur'an, in Pickthall's translation, says: "O ye who believe! Fasting is prescribed for you, even as it was prescribed for those before you, that ye may ward off (evil)."
The aim it names is to ward off evil, not to lose weight, and the same passage excuses those who are sick or traveling, who make up the days later.

The prophet Isaiah, in the King James Bible, asks what kind of fast God wants: "Is not this the fast that I have chosen? to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, and to let the oppressed go free."
There, a fast is measured by justice. Fourth, holding both.

teach.h: IS NOT THIS THE FAST THAT I HAVE CHOSEN?
teach.b: You can read the health studies with a skeptical eye and still honor the people nearby who fast for reasons no study measures: a Muslim neighbor in Ramadan, a Jewish friend on Yom Kippur, Christians keeping Lent in their own ways, seasons this path first met in its opening year.

how: Muslims fast from dawn to sunset during Ramadan, Jews fast on Yom Kippur, and Christians keep Lent in different ways; each tradition gives its fast a religious meaning and makes allowances, for example for the sick.

o: a diet plan proven to add years to nearly everyone's life
a week of eating only fruit and vegetables to cleanse the body
going without food, which religious traditions do for meaning first

p: that ye may ward off evil
to let the oppressed go free

s: research has settled that fasting is the best way to lose weight
the evidence is mixed; some readers of the research see little difference from simply eating less.
the Qur'an excuses the sick and travelers from fasting at that time
the same passage says they make up the days later.
in Isaiah, a fast is measured by how hungry you get
Isaiah's fast is to loose the bands of wickedness and let the oppressed go free.

games.q: you're Isaiah, and the people ask why God hasn't noticed their fasting. what fast do you say God has chosen?
o: a longer fast, with no water.
loosing the bands of wickedness and freeing the oppressed.
fasting in public so others see.
games.why: Isaiah answers with justice: "to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, and to let the oppressed go free."

practice: Notice your own appetite right now, hungry, full or in between, without doing anything about it.

Then bring to mind one person who keeps a fast, or one tradition's fast you've heard of, and what honoring it might look like: not eating in front of them, asking when they break the fast, learning the season's name.
Hold them in mind, kindly, and rest with the breath.

wordCard.voice: Fasting. The health research is mixed. Religious fasts put meaning first: warding off evil, and loosing the bands of wickedness. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic, from Qur'an 2:183: fasting, the word Pickthall renders "fasting" in "fasting is prescribed for you."

carryVoice: Your line: meaning first. A fast can be measured by more than a scale. Rest well.
